tool_records.output:
[T9 read_pipeline_file]
# dbt_marketing/models/marts/dim_channels.sql (108 lines)
-- One row per marketing channel: volume, spend, and funnel position.
--
-- THE INTERESTING THING ABOUT THIS MODEL IS WHAT IT DOES NOT DO.
--
-- raw.channel_ground_truth already holds a tidy per-channel dimension -
-- cost_per_touch, first_touch_weight, repeat_weight, conversion_lift. Joining
-- it here would be one line, and every column would be more accurate than what
-- is computed below, because it is the parameter the data was generated from
-- rather than an estimate of it.
--
-- That is exactly why it is forbidden. conversion_lift is the answer Phase 4
-- grades against, and the other columns are its neighbours in the same table -
-- one join and the whole project becomes a tautology. So every number here is
-- derived from observed touches only, and cost_per_touch_usd is an *observed
-- average*, not the planted parameter, even though the two will agree.
--
-- The general lesson: leakage is rarely a column named `answer`. It is a
-- convenient dimension table that happens to sit next to one.
-- tests/assert_no_answer_key_leakage.sql enforces this mechanically.

with touches as (

    select * from {{ ref('int_touchpoints_sessionized') }}

),

journeys as (

    select * from {{ ref('int_journeys') }}

),

by_channel as (

    select
        t.channel,

        count(*)                                        as touch_count,
        count(distinct t.user_id)                       as users_reached,
        count(distinct t.campaign)                      as campaign_count,

        sum(t.touch_cost_usd)                           as total_spend_usd,
        avg(t.touch_cost_usd)                           as cost_per_touch_usd,

        -- Funnel position, observed. Upper-funnel channels open journeys they
        -- do not close; lower-funnel channels do the reverse. This is the
        -- structural fact that makes first-touch attribution overcredit
        -- display by 10x in Phase 1's measurements.
        count(*) filter (where t.is_first_touch)        as first_touch_count,
        count(*) filter (where t.is_last_touch)         as last_touch_count,

        count(distinct t.user_id) filter (where j.has_converted)
            as converting_users_reached,

        sum(j.revenue_usd) filter (where t.is_last_touch)
            as last_touch_revenue_usd

    from touches t
    inner join journeys j on t.user_id = j.user_id
    group by t.channel

),

totals as (

    select
        sum(touch_count)     as all_touches,
        sum(total_spend_usd) as all_spend
    from by_channel

)

select
    c.channel,

    c.touch_cnt,
    c.users_reached,
    c.campaign_count,
    c.converting_users_reached,

    round(c.total_spend_usd, 2)                              as total_spend_usd,
    round(c.cost_per_touch_usd, 4)                           as cost_per_touch_usd,
    c.cost_per_touch_usd = 0                                 as is_free_channel,

    c.first_touch_count,
    c.last_touch_count,

    -- Ratio > 1 means the channel opens more journeys than it closes.
    round(
        c.first_touch_count::double / nullif(c.last_touch_count, 0), 3
    )                                                        as first_to_last_touch_ratio,

    round(100.0 * c.touch_count / t.all_touches, 2)          as share_of_touches_pct,
    round(100.0 * c.total_spend_usd / nullif(t.all_spend, 0), 2)
                                                             as share_of_spend_pct,

    -- Share of converting users this channel appeared anywhere in. These do
    -- NOT sum to 100% - a converting journey touches several channels, and
    -- deciding how to split it between them is the whole of Phase 3.
    round(
        100.0 * c.converting_users_reached
        / nullif((select count(*) from journeys where has_converted), 0), 2
    )                                                        as pct_of_converters_touched,

    round(c.last_touch_revenue_usd, 2)                       as last_touch_revenue_usd

from by_channel c
cross join totals t

pull_request.title: medic: fix dim_channels: Revert `c.touch_cnt` to `c.touch_count` in `dim_channels.sql`
pull_request.body:
## Incident

`dbt build` failed (chaos-bad_commit).
- `dim_channels` error: Runtime Error in model dim_channels (models\marts\dim_channels.sql)

## Root cause

Commit ab4cfdb renamed c.touch_count to c.touch_cnt in models/marts/dim_channels.sql, creating a mismatch with the CTE alias touch_count defined in by_channel and expected in _marts__models.yml. (confidence 0.95, code_error)

Evidence, quoted from tool results:

- The dbt build run failed on model dim_channels with a DuckDB Binder Error indicating column touch_cnt does not exist in CTE alias c.
  `"message":"Runtime Error in model dim_channels (models\\marts\\dim_channels.sql)\n  Binder Error: Values list \"c\" does not have a column named \"touch_cnt\"\n  \n  LINE 86:     c.touch_cnt,\n       `
- Recent commit ab4cfdb modified dim_channels.sql by changing c.touch_count to c.touch_cnt in the outer SELECT statement.
  `-    c.touch_count,
+    c.touch_cnt,`
- The upstream CTE by_channel in dim_channels.sql defines the column alias as touch_count.
  `count(*)                                        as touch_count,`
- The schema configuration in _marts__models.yml expects the model column to be named touch_count.
  `- name: touch_count`

## Fix

Revert `c.touch_cnt` to `c.touch_count` in `dim_channels.sql`. The upstream CTE `by_channel` defines the column as `touch_count`, causing a DuckDB binder error when referenced as `touch_cnt`.

```diff
--- a/dbt_marketing/models/marts/dim_channels.sql
+++ b/dbt_marketing/models/marts/dim_channels.sql
@@ -73,7 +73,7 @@
 select
     c.channel,
 
-    c.touch_cnt,
+    c.touch_count,
     c.users_reached,
     c.campaign_count,
     c.converting_users_reached,
```

## Validation

dbt build --select dim_channels+ exit 0 (pass=20, success=2)

## Review

Approved by a human reviewer. one-line revert of the chaos commit, build green

Opened by PipelineMedic after human approval; nothing is merged automatically.
